title: What makes a complete sentence?

stages.note: A big letter starts it.

explain.say: Imagine your friend shouts: The big dog! You wait... the big dog what? Something is missing! A sentence must make sense on its own. Look at the board, it shows the four parts. The first box: every sentence starts with a capital letter.

explain.say: Now the second box lights up: who or what. That part is called the subject, the one the sentence is about. In Zara swims, the subject is Zara. Who is the subject of The cat sleeps?

explain.say: See the third box? A doing word, the verb. Zara swims. The cat sleeps. Without the verb, nothing happens, and it is not a sentence yet. Can you add a verb to The big dog?

explain.say: Last box: a full stop, the little dot that says this sentence has ended. A question ends with a question mark, and a shout with an exclamation mark. The big dog barked. Now it is complete!

explain.say: You did it! The board now sorts full sentences from bits that are missing something. Look: after lunch has no subject and no verb. Challenge: turn after lunch into a full sentence of your own!

faq.a: A sentence is a group of words that makes complete sense on its own. It starts with a capital letter, has a subject and a verb, and ends with a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark.
The subject is who or what the sentence is about, usually the one doing the action. In Zara swims, Zara is the subject.
Every sentence starts with a capital letter, even if the first word is a small one like the or it.
A fragment is a piece of a sentence that is missing something, often the subject or the verb, like After lunch or The big dog.

faq.q: Can a sentence be very short?
faq.a: Yes. Birds sing. is a full sentence: it has a subject, birds, and a verb, sing.

facts: The shortest sentences can be just two words, a subject and a verb, like Birds sing.
Ancient Greek and Latin were often written without spaces or full stops at all.

quiz.say: Which of these is a complete sentence?
quiz.show: Which of these is a complete sentence?
quiz.why: The baby laughed. has a capital letter, a subject, a verb and a full stop.

wrong.1: It has a subject but no verb.
wrong.2: There is no subject and the idea is unfinished.

quiz.say: What is the subject in: Monkeys climb trees.
quiz.show: What is the subject in: Monkeys climb trees.
quiz.why: The sentence is about monkeys, who do the climbing.

wrong.0: climb is the verb, what they do.
wrong.2: trees are what gets climbed, not who climbs.
